newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU considers further break in Iran ties.
newsitem.headline: EU considers further break in Iran ties.

text.p: The European Union is considering breaking off high-level meetings with Iran and excluding top Iranian officials from its borders, according to a proposal to be discussed by EU foreign ministers next week.
The proposal, drafted by senior political officials from EU capitals, accuses Iran of conducting state terrorism and reaffirms the suspension of the EU's "critical dialogue" policy with Tehran.
"Progress can only be made if the Iranian authorities respect the norms of international law (and) refrain from acts of terrorism," a draft statement says.

The 15-nation bloc on April 10 recalled its ambassadors and suspended its policy of trying to bring Iran closer to the West through talks after a German court found that the Iranian government was involved in the murder of Kurdish dissidents.

In practice, this meant cancellation of one relatively low-level meeting of officials in May. But the move represented a significant shift towards the United States' view that Iran should be treated as a pariah state.
U.S. officials have been touring EU capitals to discuss Iran ahead of the foreign ministers meeting in Luxembourg next Tuesday and Wednesday.
Under the proposal to be put to the ministers, the EU would suspend all bilateral visits by ministers to Iran or by Iranian officials in the 15 EU countries.

EU governments would also work together to ensure that visas were not granted to "certain senior members of the Iranian hierarchy" and that Iranian intelligence personnel were excluded from EU member states, implying possible expulsion.
Diplomats said it was not clear how many of the new measures would be agreed by the EU ministers, although there was no question of lifting the suspension of the critical dialogue.
"There are a number of states...that do not want to upset Iran," one diplomat said.
He said there was concern in some EU capitals that turning up the heat on Iran while it was preparing for elections could play into the hands of Tehran hardliners.
The ministers are expected to send their countries' ambassadors back to Iran.

The advocacy group Human Rights Watch said on Friday it had written to the EU ministers urging them to tell Iran that the resumption of normal relations was dependent on Tehran taking steps against agents murdering political dissidents.
Iranian opponents of Tehran's Moslem rulers have urged the EU to break off its remaining links with Iran and impose sanctions. They plan a large demonstration in Luxembourg on Tuesday.
In Paris, a French appeals court on Friday upheld prison sentences passed last year on two men for supplying Iran's secret services with information aimed at helping to kill opponents in France.
Mojtaba Mashhady, 39, a French citizen of Iranian origin, was jailed for seven years. Iranian Hossein Yasdenseta, 37, was given three years.
